scope: Existing staging testnet. Unchanged NEAR-only SDK and harness. No new resources.
method: Sequential control/candidate/control after all local builds and E2Es; three fresh NEAR-only wallets and 21 verified signatures per arm. Existing staging resources only.

decision.reason: Remove repeated request-local runtime parsing and overlap independent target preparation with B connection. The delayed-acceptance E2E verifies the overlap and rejection boundary.
decision.protocolExchangeDecision: Opening B with A target proof would delay the connection until the fresh root read and proof preparation finish. Keep those tasks parallel. The existing proof exchange remains necessary to derive the server contribution.

roundTrips.scope: Bound-root role-private D1 only. Excludes root creation, other D1 work and local DO SQL.

browserRequestCounts.registrationVariation: The extra request is a session-status poll. Baseline samples contain four or five polls. Candidate samples contain five.

placement.provider: Cloudflare GraphQL Workers and Durable Objects analytics
placement.queryScope: Each benchmark time window and exact deployed script versions. Adaptive sampling may omit requests.

correlations.method: Wallet object IDs are matched exactly to Cloudflare analytics. Worker requests match a script/version/time window and one-second bucket. An empty result means unavailable; multiple colos mean an ambiguous bucket.

placement.d1ObservationScope: Separate read-only API queries against the bound databases before the hosted arms. These are not per-query location traces from the setup requests.
placement.outboundProbeLimitation: Outbound trace reports the destination edge that handled a probe. Use the provider analytics for execution-location conclusions. The probe arm is excluded from latency comparisons.

limitations: Three fresh wallets per latency arm. The candidate median exceeds both controls. Small sequential samples do not establish a reliable speedup or regression.
All builds and local E2Es completed before the hosted comparison.
Yao execute HTTP time excludes funding, NEAR account provisioning and the first signature. Registration-to-first timings include those separate steps.
Provider CPU and wall values cover whole invocations. CPU differences in unchanged A preparation code show that cross-arm differences cannot all be attributed to this candidate.
Application clocks freeze during CPU work. Zero-millisecond target-preparation, B-start and decode spans do not mean zero CPU cost.
Fetch-to-headers spans include receiver processing, storage completion and transport. Stage medians from different requests cannot be added to reconstruct total latency.
Object IDs match provider analytics exactly. Worker requests match the same script version and second-level time bucket. Empty buckets are unavailable, not proof of non-execution.
The broad APAC label does not establish same-data-center D1 placement. Independent primary queries returned KIX for A, SIN for B and ICN for the Signing Worker.
Gateway D1 and backend Console-call totals are unavailable. Null counters must not be interpreted as zero. Browser Console calls are separately observed.
The 1–2 second hosted Yao setup target remains unmet.

reproduction.local: Build the five strict release Workers at the source commit. Run each localVerification command with ROUTER_AB_WORKER_BUILD_PROFILE=release.
reproduction.hosted: .artifacts/r155b-phase6o-hosted/run.py runs the frozen NEAR-only harness, two controls, the candidate and a separate probe arm. It guards and restores existing versions.
